about: Condition cards v0.1. Starting values only: every t_crit_min, action and red flag must be confirmed by the health lead against a clinical guideline. Packet sizes are engineering estimates. SAMPLE protocols written from public guidelines; NASA protocols are not public. Not medical advice. Drafted with AI assistance (Claude, Anthropic).

cards.name: Chemical eye burn
cards.nasa_basis: IMM Mars transit: top driver of evacuation
cards.t_crit_basis: Immediate irrigation is standard first aid for chemical eye exposure
no_regret: Start eye irrigation now and keep going
Note the substance and the time

protocol.what_it_is: Eye injury after contact with a chemical substance.
protocol.why_in_space: Products and operations in a closed environment can cause accidental exposures.
protocol.symptoms: Pain, tearing, redness, blurred vision, light sensitivity.
protocol.app_signals: Declared exposure; symptoms; images only as support.
protocol.onboard_tests: Visual assessment; ocular pH if strips are available and the protocol includes it.
protocol.actions_now: Remove from exposure and start immediate, abundant eye irrigation as the protocol says; do not delay it to consult Earth. Precautions depend on the substance and the risk of a penetrating injury.
protocol.red_flags: Loss or reduction of vision, corneal opacity, persistent severe pain or major exposure.
protocol.t_crit_basis: Guidelines for chemical eye injury prioritise immediate irrigation. The 5 min value is provisional, NOT a validated safety deadline.
protocol.drugs: Eye treatments only as the protocol says. No doses.
protocol.supplies: Suitable irrigation solution, protection and pH strips if available; real onboard material to be confirmed.
protocol.when_evacuate: Severe injury or vision loss: urgent assessment and evacuation if feasible.

sources.label: AAO EyeWiki, Chemical (Alkali and Acid) Injury of the Conjunctiva and Cornea

cards.name: Smoke inhalation
cards.nasa_basis: IMM Mars transit: top driver of loss of crew life
cards.t_crit_basis: Airway and oxygen come first in any inhalation injury
no_regret: Move to clean air and give oxygen

cards.name: Suspected sepsis
cards.nasa_basis: IMM Mars transit: top driver of loss of crew life
cards.t_crit_basis: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: antimicrobials within 1 hour when septic shock or high likelihood of sepsis
no_regret: Prepare the antibiotic the protocol names; give it at the checkpoint or earlier if a red flag appears
cards.symptom: Fever, fast pulse, feeling very unwell

protocol.what_it_is: Life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated response to infection.
protocol.why_in_space: Isolation and delayed consultation make the response harder; no claim of higher incidence without data.
protocol.symptoms: Fever or low temperature, fast heart rate, fast breathing, confusion, possible low blood pressure.
protocol.app_signals: Trend of vital signs and mental state; suspected infection.
protocol.onboard_tests: Temperature, blood pressure, pulse, SpO2; lab tests only if really available.
protocol.actions_now: Start the emergency protocol, assess perfusion and organ dysfunction, monitor and ask for support. In septic shock or high likelihood of sepsis, antimicrobials immediately, ideally within 1 h (SSC 2021). No doses.
protocol.red_flags: New confusion, low blood pressure, breathing difficulty, poor perfusion, rapid worsening.
protocol.t_crit_basis: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021: in septic shock or high likelihood of sepsis, antimicrobials immediately, ideally within 1 h. This is NOT a waiting time before assessment.
protocol.drugs: Antimicrobials and haemodynamic support as the mission medical protocol says. No doses.
protocol.when_earth: Remote clinical support; prioritise actions that cannot wait.
protocol.when_evacuate: Instability or organ failure: consider immediate evacuation when possible.
protocol.status: DOCUMENT REVIEW DONE / SPACEFLIGHT VALIDATION PENDING

cards.name: Suspected stroke
cards.nasa_basis: IMM Mars transit: top driver of loss of crew life
cards.t_crit_basis: Stroke care is time-critical; onboard options are limited, so the decision is about monitoring and supportive care

packet.item: Short video of face, arms, speech

cards.symptom: Face droop, arm weakness, speech change

cards.name: Suspected appendicitis
cards.nasa_basis: IMM Mars transit: top driver of loss of crew life; most common patrol-threatening case on Vanguard submarines
cards.t_crit_basis: Decision window of hours for antibiotics-first management
no_regret: Capture ultrasound frames with the onboard guide

cards.name: Kidney stone (renal colic)
cards.nasa_basis: IMM Mars transit: top driver of evacuation; HRP renal stone risk
cards.t_crit_basis: Pain control within hours; obstruction with infection is an emergency
no_regret: Give the analgesic the protocol names

protocol.what_it_is: Pain caused by a blocked ureter, often due to a kidney stone.
protocol.why_in_space: Microgravity and changes in bone metabolism may raise the risk of stones; specific evidence still to be checked.
protocol.symptoms: Severe flank pain spreading to the groin; nausea; possible blood in urine.
protocol.app_signals: Reported pain; temperature; vital signs; urine dipstick if available.
protocol.onboard_tests: Ultrasound as support if available; urine dipstick if available. On Earth, NICE NG118 recommends urgent low-dose CT for adults (not necessarily available on board).
protocol.actions_now: Record onset time, vital signs and signs of infection; pain relief as the authorised protocol says. NICE: NSAID first line if appropriate; hydration as assessed, without forcing fluids.
protocol.red_flags: Fever with suspected obstruction, no urine output, worsening condition, pain or vomiting that does not respond to treatment.
protocol.t_crit_basis: NICE NG118 gives pain-relief recommendations; it does not set a single universal time threshold in minutes for renal colic.
protocol.drugs: NSAID if appropriate; IV paracetamol if NSAID is contraindicated or not enough; opioid if earlier options are not suitable or effective, as the protocol says. No doses.
protocol.when_earth: Teleconsultation and image review when latency allows.
protocol.when_evacuate: Suspected infected obstruction, no urine output or deterioration: urgent assessment for evacuation if feasible.

sources.label: NICE NG118, Renal and ureteric stones: assessment and management

cards.name: Urinary retention or infection
cards.nasa_basis: IMM Mars transit: UTI among top drivers of evacuation
cards.t_crit_basis: Acute retention needs relief within hours

cards.name: Skin infection
cards.nasa_basis: IMM Mars transit: top driver of evacuation
cards.t_crit_basis: Reassess within 24-48 h; faster if spreading
no_regret: Mark the border with a pen
Photograph with a scale every 12 h

cards.name: Shingles (herpes zoster)
cards.nasa_basis: IMM Mars transit: top driver of evacuation; herpesvirus reactivation in 61% of ISS crew
cards.t_crit_basis: Antivirals work best when started within 72 h of rash onset

cards.name: Jugular vein thrombosis
cards.nasa_basis: Marshall-Goebel 2019: stagnant or reverse flow in 6 of 11 crew, one occlusive thrombus, no symptoms
cards.t_crit_basis: Anticoagulation decision within about a day once found; found only by scheduled ultrasound
no_regret: Repeat the scan on the other side

cards.name: SANS (eye and optic nerve changes)
cards.nasa_basis: HRP SANS risk: optic disc edema on OCT in 9 of 13 crew by day 150, only 1 visible on fundus exam
cards.t_crit_basis: Develops over weeks; found only by scheduled OCT or ultrasound

cards.name: Sleep loss and fatigue
cards.nasa_basis: Barger 2014: about 6 h of sleep per night on ISS; IMM Mars: most frequent condition
cards.t_crit_basis: Cumulative; act on a week-long trend
